name: Gaddiel
overview: Gaddiel was a male member of the tribe of Zebulun, known primarily for being one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan. His role as a spy is noted in Numbers 13:10, highlighting his participation in this significant event for the nation of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Gaddiel means 'G-d [El] is my fortune; Gad is [my] G-d,' reflecting a recognition of divine providence and blessing. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 13:10, reveals a theologically rich meaning connected to God's provision.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Gaddiel was the son of Sodi, as stated explicitly in Numbers 13:10. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Gaddiel's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as one of the twelve spies representing the tribe of Zebulun during Israel's wilderness journey. His participation in this mission was vital for gathering intelligence about the Promised Land, contributing to the collective report that influenced the Israelites' faith and obedience to God's promises. This event underscores the trust placed in him and his tribe during a pivotal moment in Israel's history.
